identity.historical_origin_or_motivation: Motivated by relaxing the usual m_L = m_R assumption in inelastic dark matter while preserving attractive relic-density and experimental features.

long_lived_particles: chi_star may be long-lived on detector scales depending on parameters

standard_model_targets: electrically charged SM fermions through dark-photon kinetic mixing
SM Higgs through the scalar portal term (assumed decoupled for phenomenology)
dark_sector_couplings: diagonal elastic A_prime couplings
off-diagonal inelastic A_prime coupling between chi and chi_star
Yukawa couplings y_L and y_R to S
interaction_operators: kinetic mixing between U(1) prime and hypercharge
Yukawa Majorana mass terms from S
Dirac mass term between chiral dark fermions
annihilation_channels: chi chi and chi chi_star annihilation through A_prime to SM fermions
elastic and inelastic annihilation contributions in freeze-out
decay_channels: chi_star decays to chi plus SM fermions through off-shell A_prime
A_prime decays to dark fermion pairs when kinematically allowed
interactions.cp_structure: CP-conserving benchmark; complex phase would change the inelastic channel to p-wave
interactions.flavor_structure: two chiral dark fermions with equal U(1) prime charge

theory.notes: The paper presents a gauge-invariant anomaly-free U(1) prime extension with fermions, a singlet scalar, a dark photon, kinetic mixing, and a Higgs portal term.

symmetries.stabilizing_mechanism: The lighter Majorana state is treated as the stable DM particle; the exact low-energy stabilizing remnant is not explicitly named in the local text.

symmetries.name: U(1)'
symmetries.breaking: spontaneously broken by the singlet scalar S acquiring a vev

mechanisms: thermal freeze-out through dark-photon-mediated annihilation
elastic annihilation of Majorana ground states
inelastic coannihilation involving the excited state when not Boltzmann suppressed
production.notes: The paper computes epsilon values required to reproduce the observed DM abundance and identifies allowed thermal freeze-out windows.

phase_transitions: U(1)' spontaneous breaking by singlet scalar vev

phase_space.notes: The model is treated as thermally produced cold particle dark matter.

core.description: Dark U(1) prime coupling alpha_prime = g_prime^2/(4 pi); benchmark alpha_prime=0.5.

core.name: kinetic mixing
core.description: Kinetic mixing controlling coupling of A_prime to SM fermions and fixed by relic-density requirement along benchmark curves.

derived.description: Relative contribution of inelastic interactions to the relic abundance integral.

validity_domain.condition: Most plots use m_A_prime = 3 m_chi and alpha_prime = 0.5.
The present work only considers m_A_prime > m_chi so pure dark-sector annihilation to A_prime A_prime is forbidden.
The scalar sector is assumed to decouple from phenomenology through sufficiently small Higgs portal coupling and/or heavy radial mode.
For m_A_prime much smaller than m_Z, only the photon portal is relevant.

global.description: The benchmark sets the complex phase in the Dirac mass to zero, corresponding to CP conservation in the dark sector.
The chiral fermions carry the same U(1) prime charge, making the extension anomaly-free in the setup.
The singlet scalar sector is assumed not to drive the studied phenomenology.
Kinetic mixing is chosen so the thermal freeze-out calculation reproduces the observed DM abundance.

dominant_uncertainties: benchmark-dependent allowed regions
scalar-sector decoupling assumption

warnings.warning: Do not assume the elastic coupling vanishes as in traditional iDM; niDM is defined by nonzero left-right asymmetry and relevant elastic annihilation.
Mass windows and kinetic mixing values are benchmark dependent.
warnings.mitigation: Use the full model equations before extrapolating outside the stated parameter ranges.
